overview: Both use a 4-carbon compound to concentrate CO2, but they separate this step from the Calvin cycle in different ways — space versus time.
genZNote: C4 plants split the job between different cells at the same time. CAM plants split the job between night and day in the same cell.

aspects.label: How CO2 Fixation Is Separated
aspects.valueA: Spatial separation — CO2 fixation happens in mesophyll cells, Calvin cycle in bundle sheath cells, at the same time of day.
aspects.valueB: Temporal separation — CO2 is fixed at night and the Calvin cycle runs during the day, in the same cells.

aspects.label: When Stomata Open
aspects.valueA: Stomata open during the day, like most plants.
aspects.valueB: Stomata open only at night to minimise water loss, staying shut during the hot day.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: CAM stands for Crassulacean Acid Metabolism, named after the plant family Crassulaceae where it was first studied.
overlay.memoryTrick: C4 = separates fixation by space (different cells). CAM = separates fixation by time (night vs day).
overlay.commonMisconception: CAM plants do not photosynthesise at night — they only fix CO2 into an acid at night; the actual light-dependent Calvin cycle still runs during the day.
